data.text: In principle decisions that are spent, and tasks that are implemented or bugs, should not be deleted - we would like to be able to replay the chat, requirements, and logs, fold them, and regenerate the project from scratch, just by the chat and combined requirements, decisions, etc.

data.alternatives: Delete spent decisions and finished tasks to keep the queue small (rejected: loses the requirements trail replay and seed need). Allow delete on fold (rejected: fold silently dropped needs). Rewrite the log on re-record (rejected: unauditable). Archive spent records outside the log (rejected: a second source of truth).
data.consequences: The log and views only grow; size is managed by folding the VIEW (briefs, snapshots, cuts), not the records. Removal commands (ddflow remove and the like) must tombstone, and any that deletes is a bug. Privacy corrections need the auditable redaction event. Every new event kind needs a tombstone path, not a delete.
data.context: Operator 2026-10-23: 'In principle decisions that are spent, and tasks that are implemented or bugs, should not be deleted - we would like to be able to replay the chat, requirements, and logs, fold them, and regenerate the project from scratch, just by the chat and combined requirements, decisions, etc.' The operator answered YES to recording this as a decision and to adding a replay round-trip test. Regeneration (D-seed-extract, P-seed-extract) is only as good as the records that survive.
data.decision: Closing, abandoning, folding, superseding and forgetting are STATE CHANGES only. No agent and no command removes a record or an event: a spent decision stays (status superseded), a done task, a closed bug and an abandoned item stay with their text, links and needs. A fold carries the folded task's text, links and needs into the keeper (DX-fold-carries-needs). Event kinds are tombstoned, never deleted (D-DEP-Q11). A decision extension files a new record and never edits the old one (B-decision-extends-mutates-old-record). The one sanctioned exception is REDACTION: where private text (an address, a secret) was recorded, it may be removed from the log, and the removal must itself be an auditable event naming what was redacted and why, never a silent rewrite (D-event-log-redaction-forward; bug B-memory-rerecord-keeps-old-text-in-log: a memory re-record must not leave the old private text where redaction is required). Enforced by a replay round-trip test (DX-replay-roundtrip): replaying the log from scratch gives the live folded state and no record or event id disappears.

chunk_findings.detail: The no-deletion loop only tests whether a sampled prefix has IDs missing from the final fold (`ids - final[name]`). A record that is deleted and later re-created with the same ID is never reported. Example: event 1 adds item `x`, event 2 deletes `x`, event 3 adds `x`; `final` again contains `x`. With 3 events, `_prefix_ends(3, 16)` returns `[1, 2]`; at end 1, `earlier["items"]` contains `x` and `final["items"]` contains `x`, so the subtraction is empty. Thus `check` returns no problem even though `x` was absent after event 2, violating the stated “a record present after N events must still be present after N+k” guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py: record disappearance check in `check`

chunk_findings.detail: The verification only looks at selected prefixes. With the default `CHECKPOINTS=16` and 32 events, `_prefix_ends(32, 16)` returns only even indices `[2,4,...,30]`. A record created at event 3 and deleted at event 4 never appears in any sampled prefix, so the deletion is invisible: every sampled `earlier` is either before creation or after deletion, and `final` also lacks the ID. The module doc claims “nothing the log once recorded may disappear,” but this sampled check cannot satisfy that; it misses records that exist only between sample points.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py: `_prefix_ends` + `check` sampling

chunk_findings.detail: The `history` fixture runs `_ok(repo, "init")` before `snapshots` is populated, so the first captured event-id set is only after `task add A`. The later invariant check `itertools.pairwise(snapshots)` therefore has no earlier snapshot containing the init event(s). A log implementation that dropped the `init` event between `init` and the first `add A` would still pass `earlier <= later` because the earliest snapshot already lacks it, and `rt.check` would also not detect it because `events`/`live` are computed from that already-mutated final log. This falsifies the stated “no event id of an earlier step is gone from a later one” guarantee for the initial step.

chunk_findings.detail: The no-deletion loop only rejects IDs present in an earlier fold but absent from the final fold. A record that is removed and later re-created under the same ID is never reported. Given events `[add x, delete x, add x]` and a live State whose final `items` contains `x`, `_prefix_ends(3, 16)` returns `[1, 2]`; after event 1 `earlier["items"]` is `{x}` and `final["items"]` is `{x}`, so the subtraction is empty and `check` returns `[]`. The `x` record did disappear after event 1, but the deletion is invisible because the final fold has the same ID. This remains unfixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:check

chunk_findings.detail: The default sampler misses transient records. For 32 events with `checkpoints=16`, `_prefix_ends(32, 16)` returns `[2, 4, ..., 30]`. A record created at event 3 and deleted at event 4 is absent from `final` and is not present in any sampled prefix: prefix 2 is before creation, prefix 4 is after deletion. No `gone` ID is computed and `check` returns no problem. Since `ddflow replay --verify` uses the default of 16, the tool can report success despite the deletion the feature is meant to catch. The doc's caveat documents the limitation but does not make the verification satisfy the stated intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:_prefix_ends/check

chunk_findings.detail: The only event-id check is duplicate detection (`if ev.id and ev.id in seen`). There is no check that an event ID the log once recorded is still present, and the function receives only the current `events` list. If a buggy command removes event id `add-x` from a two-event log before verification, `events` becomes `[init]` and `live` is `fold([init])`; rebuilt equals live, no duplicate is seen, and `check` returns `[]` even though that event ID disappeared. This contradicts the module's claim that it finds "a command removing an event."
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:check

chunk_findings.detail: With default `CHECKPOINTS=16`, `_prefix_ends` for 100 events returns endpoints `6,12,...,96`. If a record is created at event 2 and then deleted at event 3, `live=fold(events)` and `rebuilt` both lack it, `differing_fields` is empty, and no duplicate event id exists; since the first sampled prefix is after the deletion, every checked earlier state also lacks the record and `check` returns `[]`. Thus `ddflow replay --verify` falsely reports a clean run for a permanent record deletion that violates the stated “present after N events must still be present after N+k” guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: `_prefix_ends` is documented as returning “at most `checkpoints` sampled prefixes”, but `step = max(1, n // checkpoints)` can produce more endpoints than `checkpoints`. For `n=10, checkpoints=6`, `step=1`, and the returned list is `[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]` (9 prefixes). For `n=1999, checkpoints=1000` it returns 1998 prefixes, breaking the upper-bound contract and potentially causing unexpectedly expensive near-exact folding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The `observe` closure uses `len(now) > len(seen)` and `len(seen) > len(now)` to decide when to update or report deletions. This misses a deletion whenever one record is replaced by another in the same collection because the collection's length is unchanged. Given two events where the observed state after event 1 is `items={'A': ...}` and after event 2 is `items={'B': ...}`, both lengths are 1; neither condition is true, so `seen` never drops `A` and `vanished([event1, event2])` returns `[]`. Record `A` disappeared at event 2, violating the module's stated no-deletion check and causing `ddflow replay --verify` to report success for a fold that drops a record.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:vanished

chunk_findings.detail: The regression probe for the prior delete-then-recreate bug only calls `rt.vanished(events)` (and the transient test similarly calls `rt.vanished(events)`); it never calls the public `rt.check(events, live)` path or `replay --verify`.  If `rt.check` regresses to the old compare-against-final-fold behavior, the input `add x; delete x; add x` still yields no problem, yet this suite remains green: `test_a_fold_that_drops_a_record_is_caught` still sees a final absence, this test never reaches `rt.check` with the recreated event, and `test_replay_verify_runs_the_round_trip` runs on an unmutated log. The earlier HIGH defect is therefore not actually pinned by this probe.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_replay_roundtrip.py:test_a_record_deleted_and_recreated_is_still_caught

Thus `ddflow replay --verify` falsely reports a clean run for a permanent record deletion that violates the stated “present after N events must still be present after N+k” guarantee.

chunk_findings.detail: `_prefix_ends` is documented as returning “at most `checkpoints` sampled prefixes”, but `step = max(1, n // checkpoints)` can produce more endpoints than `checkpoints`. For `n=10, checkpoints=6`, `step=1`, and the returned list is `[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]` (9 prefixes). For `n=1999, checkpoints=1000` it returns 1998 prefixes, breaking the upper-bound contract and potentially causing unexpectedly expensive near-exact folding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: `vanished.observe` only records newly seen ids when `len(now) > len(seen)`, and only reports a disappearance when `len(seen) > len(now)`. If an event deletes record `"a"` and creates record `"b"` in the same collection, the collection length is unchanged. For event 1 ending with `sessions = {"a": recA}` and event 2 ending with `sessions = {"b": recB}`, at event 2 both length checks are false, so `"a"` is not reported and `seen` still contains stale `{"a"}`. `ddflow replay --verify` therefore returns a clean run even though a record was permanently dropped. The exact check must diff the previous id set against the current id set regardless of lengths, not use length comparisons as a gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: `events = _log(repo).read_all()` returns `Event` objects (the test itself accesses `.kind`, `.subject`, `.lamport` on them), but the new call `rt.check(events[:-1], live, from_bytes=events)` passes that list of event objects to a parameter named and intended for raw log bytes. The assertion then looks for a problem containing `"bytes"`. A correct `rt.check` will try to decode or compare those values as bytes and raise `TypeError`/`AttributeError` when it receives an `Event` object, so this regression test fails on its own input rather than exercising the missing-event detection path. It should pass the raw bytes from the log, not `read_all()`’s decoded `Event` list.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_replay_roundtrip.py:test_an_event_missing_from_the_read_is_reported

chunk_findings.detail: When `out.data["files"]` is non-empty, the function returns `FAIL` if `out.data["roundtrip"]` has problems, but it passes `out.body(("files",))` as the structured output body; that body only includes `files` and never includes `"roundtrip"`. The no-files branch explicitly adds `"roundtrip": out.data["roundtrip"]`. Given a `replay --verify` that produced files and had verification problems, the command exits non-zero while the structured response body omits the reason, so callers relying on the body cannot see what failed.

chunk_findings.detail: The problem message builds the singular noun by stripping the final character with `f"{name[:-1]} {rid} disappeared..."`. For `research` this emits `researc`, and for `memories` it emits `memorie`. Given a log where event 1 creates a `research` record `R1` and event 2 removes it, `check(events, live)` returns the user-facing problem `"researc R1 disappeared from the state at ..."`, which is not the correct collection name. This is a generated-output defect, since the replay round-trip checker’s failure text now misnames those collections.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/replay_roundtrip.py:vanished observe

chunk_findings.detail: In `vanished.observe`, `now` is the `dict_keys` view from `getattr(st, name).keys()`, so `seen - now` evaluates `set - dict_keys`. CPython rejects this direction with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'set' and 'dict_keys'`; it does not fall back to `dict_keys.__rsub__`. Any non-empty replay that folds an event with a record collection (for example one event whose folded state has `items = {"a": rec}`) crashes before a deletion problem can be reported, so `ddflow replay --verify` fails with a traceback rather than returning findings. Use `seen.difference(now)` or `set(now)` instead.
